tax-filing-stage-1.title: The Starting Point
tax-filing-stage-1.description: A login gate, one server that runs the tax math, one database that remembers the return

nodes.label: Filer Browser
nodes.explanation: The taxpayer's browser, where they sign in, answer interview questions, and enter the numbers from their W-2

nodes.label: Login
nodes.explanation: Checks the user's password and issues a session, so every request that follows carries proof of who they are — a tax return is full of sensitive data and can't be opened by just anyone

nodes.label: Tax App
nodes.explanation: A single server that runs the interview, calculates the return, and saves progress to the database

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Stores each in-progress and filed return — sensitive, persisted data tied to the signed-in user — so they can leave and come back without losing their work

tax-filing-stage-2.title: The Guided Interview
tax-filing-stage-2.description: The app server delegates to a workflow engine, a calc engine, and a refund optimizer

nodes.label: Filer Browser
nodes.explanation: A thin renderer: it draws whatever the workflow engine says to show next, instead of knowing the tax interview itself

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Handles the session and orchestrates the three engines, then saves progress to the database

nodes.label: Workflow Engine
nodes.explanation: Owns the decision of what to ask next: given the user's answers so far, it returns the next screen. The interview branches differently for every filer, and lives here so it can change with tax law without redeploying the apps

nodes.label: Calc Engine
nodes.explanation: Federal and each state's tax rules live as separate modules, so one state's change can't break another. Answers 'what is the tax given these inputs?'

nodes.label: Refund Optimizer
nodes.explanation: Scans the whole return for deductions and credits the filer qualifies for and steers toward the largest legal refund. Answers 'which inputs are we missing?'

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Stores in-progress and filed returns, tied to the signed-in user

tax-filing-stage-3.title: Producing and Filing
tax-filing-stage-3.description: A PDF service renders the forms; a queue and worker submit and retrieve through the government APIs, with a fallback store and an email service

nodes.label: Filer Browser
nodes.explanation: The taxpayer, who wants a copy of the official return and a clear answer on whether the government accepted it

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Takes the finished return, asks the PDF service to render it, and drops a filing job on the queue

nodes.label: PDF Service
nodes.explanation: Renders the exact official government forms — pixel-correct — for both the filer's record copy and the electronic transmission. Also produces paper returns to mail where no e-file API exists

nodes.label: Filing Queue
nodes.explanation: Holds 'submit this return' jobs so the user gets an instant confirmation instead of waiting on the slow IRS

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Stores in-progress returns, filed returns, and the submission status of each filing

nodes.label: E-File Worker
nodes.explanation: Pulls jobs off the queue and submits each return to the government APIs, retrying when they're slow or down, and retrieving acknowledgements

nodes.label: Fallback Store
nodes.explanation: Durably holds the fully computed return — every number and form — the moment it's ready, independent of whether an API is reachable. The worker retries from here when a system is down, so an external outage never loses a return

nodes.label: IRS / States
nodes.explanation: Government e-file APIs the worker both submits to and retrieves from (prior-year figures, acceptance acks) — often slow, sometimes offline, and for some jurisdictions absent entirely

nodes.label: Email Service
nodes.explanation: A dedicated channel that sends the submission receipt, the acceptance confirmation, and any rejection reason — its own service so a flaky mail provider can't stall the filing pipeline

tax-filing-stage-4.title: Identity and Money
tax-filing-stage-4.description: An auth service backed by SSO/OAuth and 2FA, an isolated PII vault, a payment service, and a bank integration

nodes.label: Filer Browser
nodes.explanation: Signs in with an existing identity, clears a second factor, pays the fee, and receives the refund

nodes.label: Auth Service
nodes.explanation: Proves identity before the app server trusts any request — verifies passwords or federated tokens, and enforces a second factor (2FA) on logins from new devices and sensitive changes

nodes.label: Google / Apple SSO
nodes.explanation: Identity providers the user already trusts. Via SSO/OAuth they vouch for the user — you receive a signed token, never their password — and OAuth also authorizes scoped data imports like pulling a W-2 from payroll

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Only acts on requests the auth service has verified; routes sensitive fields to the vault and money to the payment and bank integrations

nodes.label: PII Vault
nodes.explanation: An isolated, encrypted store for the crown jewels — SSNs, past returns, bank details — reachable only through a narrow, audited interface. The main database holds a token in place of the real SSN

nodes.label: Payment (Stripe)
nodes.explanation: Collects the filing fee and handles the card data so it never touches your servers — shrinking both the attack surface and the compliance burden

nodes.label: Bank / ACH
nodes.explanation: Routes the IRS-issued refund to the user's bank account, and powers 'pay with your refund' by deducting the fee before the rest is deposited. A conduit, never a reservoir

nodes.label: Database
nodes.explanation: Holds ordinary app data and tokenized references to the vault — never raw SSNs or card numbers

tax-filing-stage-5.title: Deadline Night
tax-filing-stage-5.description: A load balancer fans out to many servers and engines, with a cache and read replica

nodes.label: Filer Browser
nodes.explanation: One of millions of taxpayers all trying to file before midnight on April 15

nodes.label: Load Balancer
nodes.explanation: Spreads incoming requests across many identical app servers and routes around any that crash under load

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: One of many identical app servers handling filers in parallel during the deadline rush

nodes.label: App Server
nodes.explanation: Another identical app server sharing the deadline-night load with the first

nodes.label: Calc Engine
nodes.explanation: The tax calculation engine, also scaled out so the heavy math runs in parallel across many machines

nodes.label: Rules Cache
nodes.explanation: Holds shared tax tables — federal brackets, state rate schedules, form definitions — in memory so engines don't reload them per return

nodes.label: Filing Queue
nodes.explanation: Buffers filing jobs so a midnight surge of submissions doesn't overwhelm the IRS or block users

nodes.label: Primary DB
nodes.explanation: Handles all writes — saving progress and recording filed returns — with locks that guarantee a return is filed exactly once

nodes.label: Read Replica
nodes.explanation: A synchronized copy that serves the constant reloads of in-progress returns, keeping that traffic off the primary

nodes.label: E-File Worker
nodes.explanation: Submits queued returns to the IRS and states, retrying as they allow, and triggers the email when each is accepted

nodes.label: IRS / States
nodes.explanation: Government e-file systems that accept or reject each return, often slowly and sometimes offline
